verdict.rationale: NVIDIA's own RTX 5080 page says the card runs GPU-optimized SDKs and maximizes performance across PyTorch, Ollama, Windows ML and other inference backends. The CUDA Toolkit docs describe a GPU-accelerated libraries, compiler and runtime stack, plus NGC containers, which shows a first-party software toolchain. However, the evidence never shows an official PyTorch build or a support matrix naming this GPU or its Blackwell compute capability, and the PyTorch mention is marketing framed around inference. Community compute benchmarks show the card running compute workloads but say nothing about framework support. Missing for 10: officially documented PyTorch/TensorFlow/JAX builds supporting the RTX 5080, a support matrix listing the GPU and required CUDA versions, training-workload framework support, independent hands-on confirmation of mainstream frameworks running on it.
